The Isthmus & Capitol Square 29 places · area 1 of 7

  1. 1 Must see within The Isthmus & Capitol Square · Markets

    Dane County Farmers' Market

    America's largest producers-only farmers' market (founded 1972): on summer Saturdays some 150 Wisconsin growers and cheesemakers completely encircle the State Capitol, and everything is grown or made by the person behind the stand. Time Out ranks it among the country's best. Order: Saturday-morning cheese curds, cheese bread and in-season produce sold by the people who made them.

    Capitol Square (Saturdays Apr–Nov), Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by , , +1,

  2. 2 Must see within The Isthmus & Capitol Square · Cheese curds

    Fromagination

    A European-style cut-to-order cheese shop on the Capitol Square since 2007, showcasing award-winning Wisconsin artisan cheesemakers — the obvious place to taste the state's cheese beyond curds. Order: Cut-to-order Wisconsin artisan cheese.

    12 S Carroll St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by , , +1,

  3. 3 Must see within The Isthmus & Capitol Square

    Wisconsin State Capitol

    The 1917 Beaux-Arts capitol at the heart of the Isthmus — the only granite capitol dome in the US. Free tours cover the rotunda mural 'The Resources of Wisconsin', and the summer observation deck gives a 360° view of the lakes. A National Historic Landmark (2001).

    Look for free tours; observation deck in summer

    2 E Main St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by , ,

  4. 4 Must see within The Isthmus & Capitol Square

    Monona Terrace

    Frank Lloyd Wright's 1938 design for a civic center on Lake Monona, rejected by one vote and built only in 1997, nearly four decades after his death. The free rooftop garden is the city's best lake-and-Capitol view.

    1 John Nolen Dr, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by , ,

  5. 5 Must see within The Isthmus & Capitol Square · Taverns

    The Old Fashioned

    The Capitol Square's all-Wisconsin tavern and supper-club homage — Wisconsin beers, brandy old fashioneds and curds. Voted Madison's best cheese curds in the 2025 reader survey and named by Isthmus associate editor Linda Falkenstein among her top fish fries. Order: Beer-battered cheese curds (house recipe batter) and the Friday fish fry.

    23 N Pinckney St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by , ,

  6. 6 Must see within The Isthmus & Capitol Square · Farm-to-table

    L'Etoile

    Madison's founding farm-to-table restaurant (Odessa Piper, 1976) on the Capitol Square — two of its chefs, Piper (2001) and Tory Miller (2012), won the James Beard Award for Best Chef: Midwest. Time Out's Madison list calls it out for working with more than 200 local vendors. Order: The seasonal farm-to-table tasting menu, sourced from 200+ local vendors.

    1 S Pinckney St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by , ,

  7. 7 Must see within The Isthmus & Capitol Square · European

    Osteria Papavero

    An intimate Italian osteria (2006) off the Capitol Square; Bologna-raised chef Francesco Mangano advanced to James Beard Best Chef: Midwest nominee in 2023. Order: Chef Francesco Mangano's Bologna- and Tuscany-rooted Italian cooking.

    128 E Wilson St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by , ,

  8. 8 Must see within The Isthmus & Capitol Square · European

    Cento

    Capitol Square Italian in a brick-and-stained-glass historic office building; Best of Madison 2026 silver for Restaurant, bronze for Italian and Chef (Edwin Ramirez); reviewed by Isthmus, The Takeout and the Daily Cardinal. Order: Handmade pasta (gnocchi with mushrooms and breadcrumbs) and wood-fired pizza.

    122 W Mifflin St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by , ,

  9. 9 Must see within The Isthmus & Capitol Square

    Madison Museum of Contemporary Art (MMoCA)

    Free contemporary-art museum in the Cesar Pelli–designed Overture complex at the top of State Street, with a rooftop sculpture garden.

    State St (Overture Center complex), Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by ,

  10. 10 Must see within The Isthmus & Capitol Square · Breweries

    The Robin Room

    Chad Vogel's 2016 lounge that 'catapulted Madison's cocktail scene' (Imbibe); on City Cast's must-try cocktails and coziest-spots lists. Order: The Jasmine (gin, Campari, Cointreau, lemon) or a seasonal house cocktail.

    821 E Johnson St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by ,

  11. 11 Worth the detour within The Isthmus & Capitol Square · Taverns

    The Plaza Tavern

    A Prohibition-era (1930) downtown tavern that invented the double-stack Plazaburger and still won't reveal its sauce; on City Cast's oldest-restaurants and best-dive-bars lists, a Daily Cardinal 'bite of the week'. Order: The Plazaburger with the secret sauce (since 1963–64).

    319 N Henry St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by , , +1,

  12. 12 Worth the detour within The Isthmus & Capitol Square · Breweries

    Great Dane Pub & Brewing Co.

    Madison's flagship brewpub since November 1994, in the NRHP-listed Fess Hotel (1858) at Doty & King; UpNorthNews readers' #1 Madison brewery 2025. Order: House-brewed Good Dog IPA or Black Earth Porter in the 1858 Fess Hotel.

    123 E Doty St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by , , +1,

  13. 13 Worth the detour within The Isthmus & Capitol Square

    Orpheum Theater

    A 1927 Rapp & Rapp movie palace a block from the Capitol — Art Deco outside, French Renaissance within — still a live-music hall; on the National Register.

    216 State St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by , ,

  14. 14 Worth the detour within The Isthmus & Capitol Square

    Wisconsin Veterans Museum

    Free state museum on Capitol Square tracing Wisconsin's military history from the Civil War (including Old Abe, the war eagle) to the present. The state has bought the building to replace it with a new five-story museum — check before visiting as construction nears.

    30 W Mifflin St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by , ,

  15. 15 Worth the detour within The Isthmus & Capitol Square

    Gates of Heaven Synagogue

    Wisconsin's first synagogue (1863, August Kutzbock) — among the oldest surviving in the U.S.; moved to James Madison Park in 1971 to escape demolition.

    302 E Gorham St (James Madison Park), Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by , ,

  16. 16 Worth the detour within The Isthmus & Capitol Square

    Tenney Park & the Tenney Lock

    O.C. Simonds' 1899 park — 'Madison's prettiest place to skate' on the lagoon (Isthmus) — and the Yahara's busiest boat lock; NRHP-listed city landmark.

    1414 E Johnson St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by , ,

  17. 17 Worth the detour within The Isthmus & Capitol Square · Supper clubs

    Tornado Club Steak House

    Off the Capitol Square, an old-school supper-club steakhouse with classic service — 2012 James Beard Best Chef Tory Miller's date-night pick, and runner-up for Madison's best old fashioned in the 2025 reader vote. Order: Barrel-aged brandy old fashioned and old-school steakhouse steaks.

    116 S Hamilton St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by , ,

  18. 18 Worth the detour within The Isthmus & Capitol Square · Pizza

    Ian's Pizza

    The late-night State Street slice shop that made mac-and-cheese pizza a Madison rite of passage. On Time Out's Madison restaurant list and its best-things-to-do roundup. Order: Mac n' cheese pizza by the slice, served until 2:30am.

    100 State St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by , ,

  19. 19 Worth the detour within The Isthmus & Capitol Square · European

    Essen Haus

    A Bavarian 'trinken halle' on East Wilson with 16 German taps, the passed-around glass boot, lederhosen-clad servers and live polka every Friday and Saturday — Madison's German-immigrant roots, played loud. Order: Two-liter glass beer boots of German tap beer, soft pretzels with mustard; weekend oompah.

    514 E Wilson St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by , ,

  20. 20 Worth the detour within The Isthmus & Capitol Square · Taverns

    Tipsy Cow

    Burger-and-whisky bar at the point of King and Main off the Square; bronze for Cheese Curds and Burger and a Best Bar medal in Best of Madison 2025; on UpNorthNews' best-curds list. Order: Beer-battered curds with Tipsy sauce; Wisconsin butter burger.

    King St at Main St, Capitol Square, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by , ,

    César Pelli's 2004 performing-arts center at the top of State Street — Overture Hall, the restored Capitol Theater and, next door, the Madison Museum of Contemporary Art.

    201 State St, Madison, WI 53703

    Madison Children's Museum

    A hands-on museum off the Capitol Square, rebuilt green with the year-round 'Rooftop Ramble' garden (chickens included) — named one of the top five US children's museums by Parents magazine.

    100 N Hamilton St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by ,

  23. 23 Worth the detour within The Isthmus & Capitol Square · Farm-to-table

    Graze

    Tory Miller's more casual, glass-walled sibling to L'Etoile on the Square (opened 2010), still farm-sourced; Madison Magazine marked its 15th year. Order: Seasonal farm-to-table gastropub plates with a view of the Capitol.

    1 S Pinckney St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by ,

  24. 24 Worth the detour within The Isthmus & Capitol Square · Pizza

    Lucille

    A tri-level King Street pizzeria and cocktail bar in the old Isthmus building (2016), with a weekly jazz night; in Travel Wisconsin's first-timer's guide to eating in Madison. Order: Wood-fired pizza and craft cocktails; Wednesday-night live jazz.

    101 King St, Madison, WI 53703

How we choose

Every place is recommended by named sources (review-aggregator star ratings never count as the recommender), pinned to its door from a published coordinate, and status-checked. Closed places stay, flagged, so you know they’re gone.

Must see
The places to plan a visit around — graded within each area, not across the city.
Worth the detour
Strong picks, worth going out of your way for.
Deep cut
For the curious: smaller, odder, more local.

Within each area, places are ordered by tier, then by number of named sources — never by popularity. No ratings, prices or opening hours are shown, because the guide doesn’t hold verified ones.

66 sights and 90 places to eat across Madison — the Capitol Square isthmus, the UW campus, the east and west sides — plus Middleton, Verona, the Dane County towns and the classic day trips (Taliesin, New Glarus, Devil’s Lake), each traceable to the source that named it. The canon is Wisconsin’s own: squeaky cheese curds, the Friday fish fry, supper clubs and the brandy old fashioned, the Dane County Farmers’ Market, Babcock Hall ice cream, Hmong & Lao kitchens and New Glarus beer.

How this guide was made

How the cuisine filters were policed

Every food card names a specific dish — a cuisine label alone doesn’t qualify. Madison’s canon is Wisconsin’s own: fresh and fried cheese curds, the Friday fish fry, supper clubs and the brandy old fashioned sweet, the producer-only Dane County Farmers’ Market on the Capitol Square, Babcock Hall ice cream, brats and butter burgers, the city’s Hmong and Lao kitchens, and New Glarus beer. Kringle is a Racine tradition — where Madison has no standout, the gap is stated rather than filled. A cuisine tag names the kitchen’s own tradition, never one dish it happens to serve.

Web-searched and fact-checked

Every place is traceable to at least two credible sources (or one institutional authority such as the James Beard Foundation or the National Park Service) — the Wisconsin State Journal, The Cap Times, Isthmus, Madison Magazine, WPR, Travel Wisconsin, Destination Madison and vetted creators — recorded in data/sources.json. Every coordinate is verified into data/geocodes.json and every place status-checked. Yelp/TripAdvisor never count toward the two-source bar.
